en: Where is grandmother going right now?
She is going to the park for a walk.
No, grandfather is resting at home.

bg-d-03-01.why: The speaker replies '공원에 산책하러 가세요' (She is going to the park for a walk).
The speaker replies '할아버지께서는 집에서 쉬세요' (Grandfather is resting at home).

bg-d-03-01.hint: Grandmother is going to the park.
bg-d-03-01.why: 가다 has no batchim, so attach -세요 → 가세요.

bg-d-03-01.q: Your friend asks where the teacher is going. Reply that the teacher is going to the classroom using 선생님 and 가세요.
bg-d-03-01.why: When honoring someone senior, attach -세요 to 가다.

items: Use -(으)세요 when a senior person is the subject of the sentence
Form natural honorific questions and answers about senior family members

en: Is the boss in the office right now?
No, he is having a meal at a restaurant.
Which restaurant did he go to?
He went to the Korean restaurant in front of the office.

bg-d-03-02.q: Where is the boss right now?
bg-d-03-02.why: The speaker answers '지금 식당에서 점심 드세요' (He is having lunch at a restaurant).

bg-d-03-02.q: What is the boss doing at the restaurant?
bg-d-03-02.why: The phrase '점심 드세요' means having lunch, said politely about someone senior.

bg-d-03-02.hint: The boss is at the restaurant.
bg-d-03-02.why: Use 계시다 instead of 있다 when indicating the presence of someone senior.

bg-d-03-02.q: Your colleague asks if the teacher is in the office. Reply that the teacher is present using 선생님 and 계세요.
bg-d-03-02.why: The honorific equivalent of 있다 for people is 계시다 → 계세요.

items: Use dedicated honorific vocabulary like 계시다, 드시다, 진지, and 댁
Avoid using plain forms like 있다 or 밥 when speaking about someone senior

en: She is seventy years old this year.
Is her health okay these days?
Yes, she exercises every day, so she is very healthy.

bg-d-03-03.why: They ask '연세가 어떻게 되세요?' and discuss her health.

bg-d-03-03.q: How does grandmother maintain her health?
bg-d-03-03.why: The speaker states '매일 운동하셔서 아주 건강하세요' (She exercises every day, so she is very healthy).
Use 연세 instead of 나이 to inquire politely about a senior person's age.

bg-d-03-03.q: Ask politely where someone senior's home is using 댁이 and 어디세요.
bg-d-03-03.why: Use 댁 for 집 and 어디세요 for 어디예요 when addressing someone senior.

items: Rewrite both nouns and verbs into honorifics to keep sentence style consistent
Politely ask about an elder person's age, home, and health

ko: 저는 학교 근처에 살아요. 선생님께서는 어디 사세요?
en: Teacher, please sit on this comfortable chair.
Thank you. Minsu, where do you live?
I live near the school. Where do you live, Teacher?
I also live in an apartment near the school.

bg-d-03-04.q: Where does Minsu invite the teacher to sit?
bg-d-03-04.why: Minsu says '선생님, 편한 의자에 앉으세요' (Teacher, please sit on this comfortable chair).

options: In an apartment near the school
bg-d-03-04.why: The teacher answers '저도 학교 근처 아파트에 살아요' (I also live in an apartment near the school).

bg-d-03-04.hint: Please sit on a comfortable chair.
bg-d-03-04.why: 앉다 has batchim ㄵ, attaching -으세요 → 앉으세요.

bg-d-03-04.q: Politely ask the teacher where they live using 어디 and 사세요.
bg-d-03-04.why: 살다 drops the final ㄹ before ㅅ: 살- + -세요 → 사세요.

items: Attach -세요 to vowel stems and -으세요 to consonant stems
Properly drop ㄹ in verbs like 살다 and 만들다 when forming honorifics
